html:
In 1961 the revolutionary government of Cuba sent about a quarter of a million volunteers, many of them teenagers, into the countryside to teach adults to read. It was called the Year of Education.

The young teachers, called brigadistas, lived with peasant families and taught by lamplight. In one year Cuba reported that it had cut adult illiteracy from about a quarter of the people to a few per cent.

The campaign became a symbol of the revolution's social gains, along with free health care and schooling. It was copied in Nicaragua and other countries. It also spread the ideas of the new state of Fidel Castro and Che Guevara into every village.
sum: In 1961 the revolutionary government of Cuba sent about a quarter of a million volunteers, many of them teenagers, into the countryside to teach adults to read. It was called the Year of Education.
